deep.reconstruction: This page has no mathematics. It is an archival cover sheet or wrapper, written in pencil in a later hand (probably the editor or archivist who sorted the Nachlass, not Riemann). It reads approximately: '88l [or 88b] / Entwürfe z[ur] Abh[andlung] üb[er] [struck out: Abel'sche Functionen] das Verschwinden d[er] Θ-function (1865 Italien). / R. [or N.]' with the folio number 106 in the right margin. The label identifies the folder that follows as drafts for Riemann's paper 'Über das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen' (Crelle's Journal 65, 1866), written in 1865 during his stay in Italy. The struck-out 'Abel'sche Functionen' shows the labeller first filed the drafts under the 1857 Abelian-functions memoir and then corrected this to the vanishing-of-theta paper. The context of that paper: for a compact Riemann surface of genus p, θ(u − e) either vanishes identically or has exactly p zeros. In the latter case, e is congruent, modulo periods and the Riemann constant, to a sum of Abel–Jacobi images of p points. The paper also characterises the theta divisor via divisors of degree p−1 (Riemann's vanishing theorem). None of this content appears on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a cover label in a later hand with no mathematical content. It only confirms the known provenance of drafts for Riemann's published 1866 paper.
transcription_corrections: The second line should read 'das [or der] Verschwinden d. Θ-function', not 'der Umkehrung[?] d. Θ-function'. This matches the title 'Über das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen'.
The shelf mark '88l' may be '88b'; the final initial may be 'N.' rather than 'R.'. Both readings are uncertain.
